newsitem.title: USA: Burlington sets $53 million plant upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Burlington sets $53 million plant upgrade.

text.p: Burlington Industries Inc. said Monday it planned to spend $53 million to expand and upgrade five plants in North Carolina, Virginia and Tennessee to keep pace with growing demand for its fabrics and yarns.
The investment will create about 190 new jobs, the Greensboro, N.C.-based maker of textiles for clothing and interior furnishings said in a statement.

The company said it will install new equipment to boost production capacity about 20 percent at four Klopman Fabrics plants in Hurt, Va., Johnson City, Tenn., and Cordova and Forest City, both in North Carolina, that make synthetic fabrics for clothing and other products.
The company will also expand and modernise textured yarn production at the Mayodan, N.C., plant in its Madison Yarn division.
Burlington Industries stock rose 12.5 cents to $10.375 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
